inline_comments.comment: Dead code should be deleted, not commented out. The equivalent block was cleanly removed in `addons.tsx`; `menu.tsx` should do the same for consistency. Leaving it as a comment implies it might be re-enabled, which is misleading.

`showPanel` is still declared `async` but no longer contains any `await` expression. The `async` keyword now serves no purpose and makes the return type `Promise<void>` instead of `void`, which is misleading to callers. Remove `async`.
Same as `showPanel` in `addons.tsx`: `showSidebar` is declared `async` but has no `await` inside. The `async` keyword is now unnecessary and should be removed.

`focusOnUIElement` is called on the click path with `forceFocus: false`. Since the panel region element is an `<aside>` (not naturally focusable), `element.focus()` will silently fail and — because `forceFocus` is `false` — no `tabindex` fallback is added. The call is effectively a no-op on click. The PR description states the intent is "clicks focus controls" (i.e. focus stays on the button), so explicitly skipping the `focusOnUIElement` call on the click path would make that intent clear rather than relying on a silent failure.

Same issue as `addons.tsx`: calling `focusOnUIElement` with `forceFocus: false` on the click path will silently fail for a non-focusable `<aside>` element. If the intent is to leave focus on the button when clicked, remove the `focusOnUIElement` call from the click path and only call it from the keyboard path.

The return value of `focusOnUIElement` is silently dropped. With `poll: true` it can return a `Promise<boolean>` (when the element isn't immediately available). The existing code just above in this same `case` block explicitly chains `.then()` on the returned Promise and falls back to `document.body.focus()` on failure. This new call has no such fallback. While no fallback is strictly needed when opening the panel, using `void` (`void fullAPI.focusOnUIElement(...)`) would at least make the intentional discard explicit and consistent with the project's code style.

Same as line 385 in the `togglePanel` case: the `Promise<boolean>` returned by `focusOnUIElement` (when polling) is silently dropped. Using `void` would make the intentional discard explicit and avoid any future linter complaints about unhandled Promises.

general_comments.comment: The `showPanel` / `showSidebar` functions in `addons.tsx` and `menu.tsx` are called from two separate code paths that now behave differently: (1) the UI button's `onKeyDown` handler calls these with `forceFocus: true`, and (2) the global keyboard shortcut in `shortcuts.ts` calls `focusOnUIElement` directly (bypassing these functions entirely). This means focus-on-open logic is duplicated and split across two layers. If the focus behavior ever needs to change (e.g., adding a fallback), it would need to be updated in both places. Consider whether `shortcuts.ts` could reuse the same `showPanel`/`showSidebar` helpers, or whether both code paths could share a single `focusAddonPanel(forceFocus: boolean)` utility.
